xs-transfer(1) ​

Transfers & paths

Copy locally, push or pull remotely, and choose exactly what a path means.

SYNOPSIS ​

Transfer form
sh
xs [OPTION]... SRC [SRC]... DEST

LOCAL COPY ​

Copy contents
sh
xs -aP src/ dst/
Copy the source directory itself
sh
xs -aP src dst/

A trailing source slash selects the directory’s contents. Without it, the source basename is included. For example, copying src to an existing dst/ creates dst/src/.

Multiple local sources
sh
xs -aP notes.txt photos/ archive/

SSH PUSH AND PULL ​

Push local files to the host
sh
xs -azP src/ user@host:/backup/src/
Pull remote files locally
sh
xs -azP user@host:/data/ data/

-z compresses remote file data with zstd. It has no compression effect on local copies. A transfer may have one remote endpoint; native remote-to-remote transfers are unsupported.

LISTING ​

List immediate entries, or recurse remotely
sh
xs src/
xs -r user@host:/data/
Inspect sources without modifying the destination
sh
xs --list-only -a src/ dst/

A single source argument lists metadata. A slash lists a directory’s immediate contents; -r includes descendants. Listings show type, permissions, byte size, modification time, and names. -l adds symlink targets.

RELATIVE PATHS AND SELECTION ​

Create dst/project/file.txt
sh
xs -aR /data/./project/file.txt dst/

With -R, /./ cuts off the path prefix. --files-from selects names relative to a single source root.

NUL-delimited selection from the current directory
sh
find . -type f -print0 | xs -a0 --files-from=- ./ user@host:backup/
NOTE

With a file list, -a preserves attributes but does not imply recursive directory traversal. Add -r when selected directories should be copied recursively.

EXISTING FILES ​

Create files that are missing at the destination
sh
xs -aP --ignore-existing src/ dst/
Skip files that are newer on the receiver
sh
xs -auP src/ dst/

--existing skips new files. --ignore-existing skips existing files. -u skips a file when the destination is newer. These are batch transfer policies, not interactive conflict dialogs.
